answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the sparrow hash is checked against the cipher checkpoint at intake, the wharf audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 83 aliases cost 209 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
